title: Every stage answers for itself (R1006 slice 2)
body:
Slice 2 of `docs/plans/oracle/subcommand-flag-forwarding.md` — **OD-10 / R1006**. Completes the dispatcher half.

`index`, `fetch`, `select` and `estimate` each gain `parse_args`. `find-best-mobo <stage> --help` now prints a usage line naming that stage and a line saying what it does; an undeclared flag is rejected with the same stage-specific usage. **None of them declares a flag** — inventing one here would be work R1006 does not authorise.

**Two docstrings lose a sentence that is no longer true.** `commands/select.py` and `commands/estimate.py` both opened with "This stage is reachable from Python only, by owner ruling: the top-level parser holds no subcommand table, so `run` takes no flags and reads nothing off `args`." The first clause is false after slice 1; the second is now a property of the stage's own parser rather than of the dispatcher.

**The no-argument fallback is not deleted**, although every shipped module now defines `parse_args`. It is what makes a *future* module correct before its author has thought about flags at all; deleting it would turn an omission into a traceback.

**`tests/test_cli_stages.py` holds no list of stage names.** It walks the `find_best_mobo.commands` package — a hand-written list here would be the subcommand table OD-10 rejected, one directory over. A stage added later inherits R1006 rather than re-discovering BL-5 the way `aliases` did. It also asserts a rejected flag costs no work, by checking the data directory was never created.

Every existing `run(config, Namespace())` call still passes **unedited**: `parse_args` is a new entry point beside `run`, never a precondition of it.

21 new tests, 516 passing.

Carries a merge of the base branch so the required checks run against the tree this will land on.
